messages.author: b048c97bee0de8a7
messages.subject: Lavaan - credible software?
parts:
Hello,

I have been using Lavaan for a couple of years since I found this software is incredibly useful and helpful. I would like to use it throughout my future academic life. I also have been employing it in developing several manuscripts to publish my work to highly respected journals. Recently, I've got a comment from a professor saying that 

"Lavaan only approximates SEM and even the creator of the program himself admits that “the results of lavaan are very close … to those reported by their current commercial program” (Rosseel, 2012). If lavaan does give the same results, then there really is no concern, the problem is, you never know when it may or may not."

I was not able to make an argument to the comment. I would like to ask your advice for the matters of how much this software is reliable compared to commercial softwares.

Thank you very much for your advice!

Best regards,
Yonghwan Chang

messages.author: 671b14edc9322fa7
messages.subject: Re: Lavaan - credible software?
parts:
Hi

The same question was asked on this list a couple of months ago.

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/lavaan/Yfewh9tnH04

If you must have results that are results that are always identical to software X, then you must use software X. Because the estimation algorithms can be implemented in different ways, it is unlikely that software Y will always produce exactly same results as software X. This applies to Lavaan and all commercial software. For example, you cannot expect e.g. Mplus and AMOS to always give exactly the same result.

Mikko

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Lavaan - credible software?
parts:
On 04/01/2015 06:15 AM, Experimental study with SEM wrote:
> Recently, I've got a comment from a professor saying that
>
> "Lavaan only approximates SEM
I wonder what this means "approximating SEM".

> and even the creator of the program
> himself admits that “the results of lavaan are very close … to those
> reported by their current commercial program” (Rosseel, 2012).

Your professor clearly failed to see/understand the subtle message in
this sentence: there are indeed some (minor and major) discrepancies
between lavaan and some commercial packages. I spent a lot of effort in
trying to pinpoint the cause of these discrepancies (hint: the mimic=
option). Apart from some trivial numerical issues (like the stopping
criteria used by optimizers), it turns out there are a few mistakes (or
at least non-standard implementations) in several commercial packages.

> If lavaan
> does give the same results, then there really is no concern, the problem
> is, you never know when it may or may not."

Well, this is the thing: with lavaan (or any other open-source software
for that matter), you *can* know when there is reason for concern: you
can check the source code. Many people (including SEM experts) do.

> I was not able to make an argument to the comment. I would like to ask
> your advice for the matters of how much this software is reliable
> compared to commercial softwares.

Everywhere around the world, you will find people that simply can not
believe that an open-source software package can be reliable... It is a
free world. If they prefer to buy commercial, that is fine by me.

(PS: For what it is worth: someone just pointed out to me that lavaan
was used in a Nature article this week:
http://www.nature.com/srep/2015/150330/srep09521/full/srep09521.html)

Yves.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Lavaan - credible software?
parts:
"Lavaan only approximates SEM

I'm not sure what this is supposed to mean.  It estimates SEM parameters, just like other SEM software.  They seem to indicate that it is only a "real" SEM if it is fit to data using commercial software, which is just not true.
and even the creator of the program himself admits that “the results of lavaan are very close … to those reported by their current commercial program” (Rosseel, 2012).
I believe it can mimic results from Mplus, LISREL, and EQS (3 commercial software programs that each can give different results from each other).
If lavaan does give the same results, then there really is no concern, the problem is, you never know when it may or may not."

Replicability of results is indeed an important facet of scientific progress.  But the fact is that numerous algorithms can be designed to solve the same problem.  Each commercial SEM software package is a different of algorithms for solving (mostly) the same set of problems.  Even if they base their work on the same mathematics, they can translate equations into a program very differently.

lavaan is just as valid as any other package because it is based on the same mathematics behind SEM.  Furthermore, it includes options to mimic the algorithms of Mplus, EQS, and LISREL.  The difference about lavaan is that it is open-source, so you can actually read the program to see what is being done.  It is commerical software that requires faith, whereas lavaan is open to peer-review, making lavaan more conducive to scientific progress than commericial software.

Terry

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Lavaan - credible software?
parts:
It sounds like your reviewer either (a) has a bias against open source software, (b) has confused a particular package with the analytical method itself, as many people take LISREL to be a method and not just software, or (c) has Lavaan confused with a composite-based method, as this is the kind of complaint one encounters about composite-based methods.
     If it might help . . .the publisher Wiley is putting together an online encyclopedia on research methods called Wiley StatsRef.  I am the author of two revised articles, one titled "Structural Equation Modeling: Software."  The original, published in 2005, of. Or use did not mention lavaan, but the revision places it squarely among other packages for factor-based SEM.  If you like, I can send you a copy of the proof.
--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Lavaan - credible software?
parts:
In addition, if you run any complex model in different software you're likely to get (very, very slightly) different answers. That's true of SEM, if you compare (say) LISREL, Mplus and AMOS.   It's even more true when programs have idiosyncratic ways to calculate things - e.g the incrememental fit indices (CFI/NNFI) in Mplus are calculated differently from most other programs. 

It's also true of multilevel models. Try running a multilevel logistic model in two packages (or even, in the case of SAS, two procs within the same package) and the results don't always agree perfectly.

J
